subject: Cross-border ops add-on & Warm-standby capacity for EU primary
body:
--- Message 1 of 5 ---
From: Sofia Patel <sofia.patel@medivance.com>
To: nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@medivance.com>, Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medivance.com>
Date: 2026-08-30 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Renewal scope question — EU primary + APAC warm-standby

Hi Nikhil,

We reviewed the renewal proposal and have two items we need clarified before legal signs off: a) we want the EU region to be the primary residency for PII and patient data, and b) we'd like a warm-standby APAC node for DR / surge during APAC hours.

Specifically:
- Can you confirm the SLA/latency targets for EU primary traffic?
- If we add a warm-standby in APAC, will that change billing (committed v burst) or data residency guarantees?
- We also estimate a 30% peak token uplift during influenza season — what's the recommended capacity uplift / SKU change to cover that?

Attached our latest SOW draft with requested amendments (SOW v3).

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if easier.

Best,
Sofia
Director, Platform Ops
Medivance Health

Attachments: Medivance_SOW_v3.pdf (application/pdf)

--- Message 2 of 5 ---
From: nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai
To: Sofia Patel <sofia.patel@medivance.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-30 13:34:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Renewal scope question — EU primary + APAC warm-standby

Hi Sofia — thanks for the clear note and for attaching the SOW. High-level answers here, and I propose a short touchpoint tomorrow to align on the mutual action plan: 

1) EU primary residency & SLA: We can designate the EU region as the primary jurisdiction for all customer-controlled data; SLA targets for EU primary will match our Dedicated EU profile (99.95% uptime, p50/p95 token latency targets in the SOW). We'll call out the binding residency clause in the SOW.

2) APAC warm-standby: A warm-standby node is supported and configured as a cross-region failover. By default, standby capacity is billed as reserved standby (monthly committed SKU) if you want guaranteed warm capacity and reduced cold-start latency. We also support a lower-commit burst option billed per-token for occasional use. We should decide on a commit level (we can propose 20% of peak as standby commit to start).

3) Capacity uplift: For a 30% expected peak uplift, we recommend increasing the EU committed capacity by 25% and adding a 15–20% warm-standby commit in APAC to keep tail latency predictable during failover and overlap windows. I'll include concrete SKU numbers in the updated SOW.

I'll loop in Ben and Soojin to prepare updated pricing language and the addendum describing residency guarantees and failover behavior.

Can we do 30 minutes tomorrow at 10:00 CET?

Thanks,
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

--- Message 3 of 5 ---
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-31 08:15:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Medivance — EU primary + APAC standby (pricing draft)

Team — drafting numbers below for the SOW addendum. Using current consumption and Sofia's peak uplift note:
- Current EU commit: 600 AUs/month -> proposed EU commit: 750 AUs/month (25% uplift)
- APAC warm-standby (recommended commit): 150 AUs/month ( ~20% of peak)
- Warm-standby billing: 60% of full-rate (standby discount) while idle; full rate only applies when standby promoted to active.

Action items:
- Soojin: please add residency clause language and fallthrough routing rules (how requests are routed during failover).
- Marissa: update the SOW legal header + add rollback clause for cutover testing.
- Nikhil: confirm with customer if standby should be reserved (committed) or burst-only.

I'll attach the pricing worksheet and a short note describing failover runbook.

Attachments: Warm-Standby-SKU-Worksheet.xlsx

Thanks,
Ben
Account Solutions

--- Message 4 of 5 ---
From: nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai
To: Sofia Patel <sofia.patel@medivance.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@medivance.com>, Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medivance.com>, ben_carter@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-01 09:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Renewal scope question — EU primary + APAC warm-standby

Sofia / Tom / Elena — following our internal review, here's a concise mutual action plan we can add to the SOW addendum. Please confirm and we'll produce a redline.

Mutual Action Plan (MAP):
- Objective: Renew current Dedicated EU tenancy; add 25% committed EU capacity uplift; provision an APAC warm-standby with 150 AUs committed initially.
- Data Residency: Redwood will ensure EU region is configured as primary residency for all customer-controlled PII and model inputs; no APAC node will persist PII at rest unless explicitly allowed by Medivance in writing.
- Failover behavior: APAC warm-standby will only be used for failover or scheduled surge windows; routing uses health probes plus geo-priority policy. When promoted, standby is billed at full rate for the promotion period.
- Billing & Credits: Standby commit billed at standby SKU; if standby is promoted for >72 hours continuous, a grace credit applies for the first 24 hours of promotion (to account for testing/promotion anomalies).
- Cutover testing: We'll run a staged failover test during a mutually agreed maintenance window. Rollback steps documented in SOW addendum (Marissa to add).
- Timeline: Draft addendum in 3 business days; mutual review + redline within 5 business days; target signature within 3 weeks.

Next steps: please reply with a single-line ACK and whether you prefer standby as "reserved-commit" or "burst-only". If reserved, we'll send DocuSign addendum with the SKU worksheet.

Regards,
Nikhil

--- Message 5 of 5 ---
From: Sofia Patel <sofia.patel@medivance.com>
To: nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@medivance.com>, Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medivance.com>
Date: 2026-09-02 15:04:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Renewal scope question — EU primary + APAC warm-standby

Thanks, Nikhil — ACK on the MAP. Medivance prefers reserved-commit for the APAC standby (150 AUs/mo). One ask: can you include an appendix that lists the exact data flows (for legal) — which services store PII, for how long, and where snapshots/backups live? Elena will be the legal owner for review.

If you send the DocuSign with the SOW addendum and the Warm-Standby worksheet, we'll route to procurement this week.

Best,
Sofia

--- End of thread ---
